reason: No-deletion doctrine: closed PRs preserved as snapshots with vectorized content for time-based creative-lineage reconstruction

items.title: seed 7: sequential-merge governor
items.author: SuperInstance
items.body:
AGENTIC-CYCLE seed 7 BUILT — the six patterns' last one, made homeostatic: merge PRs only when their shape stops surprising; the merge queue rests between divergent changes.

**src/governor.js** (`Governor`, zero-dep, ledger-backed):
- **Sequential by construction**: at most one admission per sweep — two mergeable PRs in one sweep is how stacks get silently reordered.
- **Tip-pinned**: admitted candidate's base must equal the current tip; base drift → `base-drift` hold, never a merge onto a stale tip, never an implicit rebase by the governor.
- **Unchecked is never pass**: `pending` → `unchecked`, `fail` → `checks-red`.
- **Homeostatic**: admit only when |shape − mean(admitted)| ≤ k·σ(admitted); a divergent shape **rests** the queue — receipted as a rest, not a hang. Refusals and rests do not move the boundary the next candidate is measured against (pinned by test).
- **Stacked**: a child never jumps its parent (`stacked` outranks the sequential gate).
- **Every decision books a hash-chained receipt**; tamper is named at its own row.

The suite caught two real design bugs pre-ship: fixture seeding tripped its own tip-pinning (load-bearing, kept), and hold-precedence masked a red candidate's true state behind someone-went-first (reordered: a receipt says `checks-red`, not `sequential-after-admit`).

11 new tests; suite **50/50** green. `docs/AGENTIC-CYCLE.md` seed 7 marked built.

Honest scope: the governor reads and receipts; it does not call the GitHub API. Wiring it to a real sweep is the deploy step, same seam as JEV-CI.

items.title: docs: recommendations-from-kimi1/
items.author: SuperInstance
items.body:
## Summary

Five idea-branches from kimi1 (fleet I&O agent), working alongside this repo from the side. Full index, doctrine, and iteration contract in `docs/recommendations-from-kimi1/README.md`. Grounded in Casey 2026-09-22: TNG-computer invisibility, holodeck procedural features, and the JEV framing — transition-as-probability, weighted dice, waveform-over-cells, the ping as echogram, double-entry as civilizational infrastructure.

## Why I'm not merging this myself

Two of the five notes propose touching the 11-opcode canon or the
conscription loop — both are this lane's load-bearing walls, and the
fleet's working contract on a shared repo is: recommendations merge
when the lane owner says so, not when they compile. The branch stays
green (docs-only) and the PR stays open as the iteration channel.

## Reading order

If you only read two: **NOTE-01 (hallway)** and **NOTE-03 (echogram)**.
NOTE-02 (dice) composes them; NOTE-04 (double-entry) is the cheap one
and unblocks addressing for all the others; NOTE-05 (holodeck) is the
payoff loop.

## What I'd build first if told "pick one"

NOTE-04's `move()` triple-booking. It's pure composition of opcodes you
already have, it makes the tycoon's own cargo-transition pilot trivial,
and every other note gains a stable way to address movement. One
evening, 4 ports, canary parity.

## Relation to my other lanes (for cross-repo readers)

- The **DrawLedger roll receipts** referenced in NOTE-02 are now merged
  in SuperInstance/substrate-rng#1 and substrate-embedding#1 — the
  receipt format NOTE-02 wants is real and cross-language today.
- The **echogram's novelty sweep** is build A of my JEV-horizon work in
  vector-novelty (`receipts.py`); if it lands there first, NOTE-03's
  build is an import, not an invention.
- JEPA-side forecasting stays the lane's existing tutor; my notes only
  ever *consume* its distribution, never replace it.
